newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL SHARES CLOSE LOWER ON CONTINUING RINGGIT WOES.
newsitem.headline: KL SHARES CLOSE LOWER ON CONTINUING RINGGIT WOES.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed further down on Tuesday, inspite of a partial recovery on support from local institutions, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 4.89 points, or 0.54 percent, lower at 897.25.
It had hit a new 1997 low of 884.61 points, but a spurt of local institutional support helped to push it momentarily into the black at the 903.12 level.
"There has been some foreign selling here and there, but it has mostly been margin selling," said a local dealer.
Margin calls are made on bank and brokerage house clients whose loans are collateralised against stocks to top up their portfolios with cash or to sell their holdings.
Continuing uncertainty over the direction of the local currency remained the main driving force behind the foreign selling, fund managers said.
"Our main worry is the currency, that the ringgit will weaken," said the managing director of a Japanese investment fund in Singapore.
He said he had reduced the fund's exposure to Malaysian equities to "quite close to zero".
Local institutions were seen buying power and telecommunications utilities Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and Telekom Malaysia Bhd, rising 10 cents and remaining unchanged respectively.
Malayan Banking Bhd closed 30 higher at 22.00 ringgit, also on local funds support, said dealers.
The three stocks have the heaviest weighting on the index.
Overall market volume stood at 291 million shares, valued at 1,427 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 454 to 218.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract gained 16.8 points to 906.8, with 1,796 lots traded. September futures closed 17.7 points higher at 908.0 with 11 lots changing hands.
